links.comparator_used: No AI output (the text-only AI arm was a separate arm, not directly compared with the confidence score arm)
links.outcome: Radiologist AUC for lung nodule and mass detection on chest radiographs
links.effect: Combined text and AI confidence score vs no AI: AUC 0.77 vs 0.82; P = .46. Text-only vs no AI was 0.87 vs 0.82; P < .001.
links.quote: There was no difference in performance for the combined text and AI confidence score output compared with no AI (0.77 vs 0.82; P = .46) and for the combined text, AI confidence score, and image overlay output compared with no AI (0.80 vs 0.82; P = .66).

links.comparator_used: No AI output (no overlay-free AI arm was compared directly)
links.outcome: Radiologist AUC for lung nodule and mass detection, and user preference
links.effect: Text, confidence score and image overlay vs no AI: AUC 0.80 vs 0.82; P = .66. 8 of 10 radiologists (80%) preferred this interface over the other two.
links.tradeoff: Preference did not match performance: the most preferred interface gave no measurable performance gain.
links.quote: There was no difference in performance for the combined text and AI confidence score output compared with no AI (0.77 vs 0.82; P = .46) and for the combined text, AI confidence score, and image overlay output compared with no AI (0.80 vs 0.82; P = .66).

links.comparator_used: Three AI UI formats (text-only; text plus confidence score; text, confidence score and image overlay) each tested against no AI
links.outcome: Radiologist AUC and user preference across candidate AI UI formats
links.effect: Text-only improved AUC vs no AI (0.87 vs 0.82; P < .001). The other two UIs showed no difference (0.77 and 0.80 vs 0.82). 80% of radiologists preferred the text, score and overlay UI.
links.tradeoff: User preference did not correspond with performance, so choosing a format by preference alone would pick a UI that did not improve accuracy.
links.quote: Text-only UI output significantly improved radiologist performance compared with no AI in the detection of lung nodules and masses on chest radiographs, but user preference did not correspond with user performance.
